extracted.intended_audience: early-career technology transfer professionals, prospective T3 fellows, mentors, and sponsoring organizations
extracted.subtask_description: A description of the AUTM Foundation's Technology Transfer Career Training (T3) Program: a mentorship-and-training fellowship for early-career professionals or those transitioning into technology transfer, offering webinars, practical experience, networking, and institutional resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target participants / eligibility (audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program offers early career professionals or those looking to transition into careers in technology transfer an opportunity that includes formal training, networking and practical experience in this field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for individuals at the start of their technology transfer careers or those seeking a career change into tech transfer; program pairs selected applicants with mentors and provides structured learning and networking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching program goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The overarching goal of the program is to offer early career fellows unique resources and opportunities that will engage and encourage them to become the future leaders of the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design and activities should emphasize leadership development and long-term career advancement in technology transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor pairing and mentor support
rubrics_metrics.description: The program pairs selected applicants with an experienced technology transfer mentor who offers in-depth, first-hand knowledge of the complexities of the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors are provided with a roadmap and timeline to help foster the best experience; mentorship is highlighted as a top perk for fellows and valuable to mentors themselves. Contact for interested mentors: mfrale@autm.net with subject line 'T3 Mentor.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Core syllabus / curriculum topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows follow a core syllabus of educational webinars covering such topics as the fundamentals of technology transfer, invention disclosures from cradle to licensing, basic patenting, marketing, and negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum delivered via webinars and other materials to ensure grounding in the seven Fundamentals of Technology Transfer; used as the primary content framework for fellow training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to AUTM resources (membership & Practice Manual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fellow is provided a two-year AUTM membership providing access to AUTM’s Technology Transfer Practice Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership includes unlimited access to a 200+ webinar library and the Practice Manual, which serve as reference and ongoing learning resources throughout the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program experiential components / required events
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows attend AUTM’s Essentials Course, Annual Meeting and one Regional Meeting to continue building their network and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance at these events is part of the fellowship experience and is intended to provide in-person learning, networking, and professional exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized training while remaining employed
rubrics_metrics.description: Individualized training without leaving current position
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is structured to allow fellows to participate and receive tailored training without requiring them to leave their current jobs; suitable for working professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid delivery model
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinar and live training hybrid method for deeper understanding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines online webinars and live training events to balance flexibility and immersive, interactive learning opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational tailoring / employer-specific customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations able to tailor program to meet specific needs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host organizations or sponsoring offices can adapt aspects of the fellowship to address local priorities or gaps in skills/knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking / peer and professional network building
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer and professional networks are established
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program activities intentionally foster peer cohorts and wider professional networks as a key outcome, enabling knowledge sharing and long-term career connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of completion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows who complete program requirements receive a certificate, which can be used to document participation and training outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation pathway: Susan Riley Keyes Memorial Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the Susan Riley Keyes Memorial Fund, the AUTM Foundation offers positions in our T3 Program to individuals from small TTO offices throughout North America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pathway targets candidates from small technology transfer offices; the fund continues Susan Riley Keyes' legacy of support, service, and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation pathway: Sponsored by Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsored by Office — If you would like to sponsor an early-stage tech transfer professional or someone interested in joining the profession, learn more here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations can sponsor employees (or prospective employees) to participate in the program as a way to develop targeted skills through courses, webinars, mentorship and more.
